title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
summary: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" and were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.

title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
summary: The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-lofty goal of Elon Musk's rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists.

title: Judge blocks FCC from early license review for ABC, which network says has had a chilling effect
summary: A federal judge on Wednesday blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses, agreeing with the network that the Trump administration was chilling the network's free speech rights.

title: King tides and strong waves destroy part of Pacifica pier as officials warn of coastal flooding
summary: King tides combined with powerful waves destroyed part of a pier in Northern California on Wednesday, and officials warned more beachfront homes are at risk of flooding.

title: Nvidia CEO's comeback fuels debate over misogyny and impunity for the rich and powerful
summary: Just over a year ago, the chief executive officer of an Ohio tech company was forced to resign when he was caught on video embracing an employee at a Coldplay concert. The CEO of McDonald's was among several pushed out over a consensual relationship at the height of the #MeToo movement.

title: Small plane crash off Mississippi coast kills extended family of 6 on fishing trip
summary: Authorities are investigating why a small plane carrying six members of a Florida family crashed off the Mississippi coast on Tuesday. They were returning home from a fishing trip, relatives say.

title: Thanksgiving holiday plagued by heavy rain, wind and flooding across much of the U.S.
summary: Much of the U.S. is facing foul weather for Thanksgiving, with a storm in the East forcing the postponement of Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade and strong winds and king tides prompting flood warnings and knocking out part of a city pier in the West.

title: What are king tides? These exceptionally high tides are increasingly flooding coastal communities
summary: King tides are the highest tides of the year, and they are increasingly flooding coastal communities as sea levels rise.

title: Judge declines to issue a long-term ban on taxpayer-funded, pro-Trump ads critics called propaganda
summary: A federal judge on Wednesday sided against Democrats on the federal government's taxpayer-funded ads that promoted partisan messages and President Donald Trump ahead of the midterm elections, declining to extend a temporary ban.

title: Trump calls GDP figures 'fake' and demands an investigation of Commerce Department
summary: President Donald Trump on Thursday accused his Commerce Department of purposely issuing incorrect economic growth figures before the midterm elections, and said he wants to launch an investigation.

title: Trump heads to Arizona next week for a high-stakes expansion of TSMC's computer chip factories
summary: President Donald Trump, who has staked his economic policy on growth in the artificial intelligence sector, will travel to Arizona on Dec. 4 to speak at the groundbreaking for a new Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. computer chip foundry, according to both the White House and the Taiwan-based company.

title: Despite political divide, Americans often 'speak in one voice'
summary: In this era of sharp American divide, politics has increasingly become a dish families work to keep off the Thanksgiving table. But in reality, data show Americans actually agree on many tough topics, spanning more than 100 policies. Lisa Desjardins spoke with two leading researchers whose counter-intuitive findings suggest our division is based on politics, not policy.

title: How Democrats' election successes could lead to new climate change policies
summary: Even though it did not play a major role on the campaign trail, with Democrats' commanding wins nationwide as well as at the state level, some environmental groups are convinced that more substantive action is just around the corner. Caroline Spears, executive director of the advocacy group the Climate Cabinet, joins Williams Brangham to discuss.

title: How women in Israel are playing larger roles in the military
summary: Israel has now been at war for the last three years alongside the United States. While women have long been at the forefront of the Israel Defense Forces, their roles are now expanding. Special correspondent Nurit Ben looks at their unique challenges.

title: Journalist's experiences highlight challenges of being a family caregiver
summary: More than 60 million Americans are caregivers for their family members, providing a wide range of needs. In November that work is recognized as National Family Caregivers Month. Richard Lui, a caregiver advocate who has directed two documentaries on the subject, joins Amna Nawaz to discuss.

title: New book focuses on how to get through life's hardest days
summary: Today much of the country is focusing on life away from work, but most of us struggle daily with the demands of work, home and the constant pings of electronics. In this episode of our "Settle In" podcast, speaker and executive coach Jovian Zayne talks with Geoff Bennett about her new book, "Soft Landings for Hard Days," a guide for how individuals can find small moments of respite and joy.

title: News Wrap: EPA reports 'zero' airborne lead in Iowa
summary: In our news wrap Thursday, the EPA is reporting "zero" airborne lead in Middletown, Iowa, a day after the Army detonated nearly five tons of toxic explosives, the Trump administration is planning for new, sharp tariffs on 14 countries, and President Trump says he told Russian president Vladimir Putin to "pull back on military aggression" in Europe.

title: Stormy Thanksgiving weather causes delays and damages for many Americans
summary: A stormy Thanksgiving day led to serious flooding, major power outages and disrupted travel plans. By Thursday evening, more than 900,000 customers were without power in at least eight states. The East Coast is grappling with a pair of storm systems affecting people from Maine to Florida. This as strong winds battered the West Coast from Oregon to California. Lisa Desjardins reports.

title: The best strategies for holiday shopping in the age of AI
summary: Americans are expected to spend more than $1 trillion on holiday shopping this year despite concerns about rising prices. PBS News digital video producer Cecilia Lallmann looks at the ways we could shop smarter this year, including with the help of artificial intelligence.

title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
summary: Gérard Depardieu, for decades one of France's most celebrated actors, has been ordered to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting a young actress, authorities said Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate case.

title: Mexico's most powerful cartels adapt as arrests and leadership battles reshape their ranks
summary: The arrest of another Mexican drug lord over the weekend added to a string of actions against cartels as Mexico intensifies its crackdown on organized crime under mounting pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump and with U.S. intelligence support.

title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons, days after ignoring U.S. President Donald Trump's offer to meet during his recent visit to Asia.

title: Zelenskyy warns of imminent major Russian attack on Ukraine's power grid
summary: Russia is preparing another major attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, logistics and critical services, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Thursday, as U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said Russian President Vladimir Putin has "shown restraint" in the war by agreeing not to use nuclear weapons.
